description: Contextual keywords (empty, member, of, a) are not built-in names, so they are legal procedure names even in a DECLARATION slot: `define empty/member/of/a ... end` defines them in the callable namespace and the subsequent calls resolve, with no ol-reserved-word and no ol-unknown-command. They are structural by POSITION only -- just after `is` for all four, and additionally in the Heritage `value of ... for key` reader for `of` -- and spec/grammar.md:380 gives the reason this is safe: "the positions that make them structural are positions no declaration can occupy, [so] taking one of these names cannot make a definition unreachable: `define of` is legal". This is the positive mirror of reserved-word-define-reserved, which raises ol-reserved-word for `define repeat ... end`, and it is the fixture that survives maintainer ruling #833: the binder/`local` sibling no longer distinguishes these four from a keyword, because binding any name is free.
